GitHub Copilot for BudgetWise (.NET 8 ASP.NET Core Web API; React TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind frontend).

**Standards:** C# PascalCase types/members, camelCase locals/parameters; meaningful focused methods, composition, C# 12, `var` when obvious, namespace-internal `using`. New code: strict TypeScript, no inline styles, Tailwind, semantic accessible HTML (ARIA/keyboard), hooks, functional reusable components. Constructor DI with appropriate lifetimes. Consistently use minimal APIs or controllers; REST plural resources, HTTP actions, `/api/expenses/{id}`, `/api/expenses?category=Food`, camelCase JSON, Content-Type, proper status codes. Typed results/`IActionResult`; Data Annotations/FluentValidation; meaningful errors; DTO records, explicit mapping, nullable references, `required`, navigation properties, property-based initialization. Built-in auth/CORS middleware; in-memory dev/test data, thread-safe collections as needed; realistic `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`. Public classes/methods require XML `<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, applicable `<exception>`; TypeScript JSDoc. Explain WHY; incomplete work uses `// TODO:` with clear descriptions; explain .NET/React concepts; beginner-friendly, clear, simple, demonstrative best practices.

**Process:** Check existing patterns first; follow conventions; add exception handling/validation; tests alongside code and update docs; maintain full-stack coherence; validate backend/forms (client-side); typed results/statuses; TODO exercises follow patterns and have tests.

**Testing:** xUnit, React Testing Library, MSW (or similar); AAA; `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; `WebApplicationFactory<T>` integration tests; mock externals; success/failure, edge/boundary, interactions (not implementation), accessibility, Testing Library `screen`.
